name: The Asia Minor Fontanesia of the Kleiner Tiergarten

location.address: Kleiner Tiergarten, east of Stromstrasse, Berlin-Moabit

access: Free, public park (Kleiner Tiergarten), open at all times.
transport: U9 Turmstrasse, about 6 minutes on foot (approximate).
verify_notes: REGISTER: Naturdenkmal 1-49/B (and twin 1-50/B at 52.525778,13.344472, about 25 m east; fold into this one entry, note both ids), Fontanesia phillyreoides, designated 1993-03-02, reasons Seltenheit and landeskundliche Gruende (rarity, local-history). Fontanesia is a rare privet-family shrub or small tree from Asia Minor; register itself names rarity as the reason. PIN: register point 52.525694,13.344167; CC0 Commons photos geotagged 2, 3 and 6 m away (52.52571372,13.34415403, file ...ND-1-49 2024-06-16 06/07/05) and for 1-50 geotagged 4 m away (...ND-1-50 2024-06-16 04/05/06). OSM node 12964352880 (natural=tree, ref 174, 52.52597,13.34434) is a park-inventory tree near 1-50, not authoritative. PHOTO CANDIDATES: Commons File:Naturdenkmal Kleinasiatische Fontanesie Kleiner Tiergarten, oestlich der Stromstrasse ND-1-49 2024-06-16 06.jpg, CC0, Leonhard Lenz, 2024-06-16 (photo pass must LOOK before approving; a shrub-form rarity may not fill a frame). No age and no girth in the register (Berlin Naturdenkmal data carries neither). Register, Wikipedia list and Wikidata all trace to the same 1993/2021 ordinance, so they count as ONE source; the independent evidence is the CC0 Commons photograph geotagged at the tree. Alive: photographed 2024-2025 by the same photographer. Photographer on Commons: Leonhard Lenz (CC0, no attribution required; record as Leonhard Lenz / Wikimedia Commons, CC0).

name: The Bosnian Maple of Gendarmenmarkt

location.address: Gendarmenmarkt, south-west of the Deutscher Dom, corner of Charlottenstrasse, Berlin-Mitte

access: Free, public square (Gendarmenmarkt), open at all times.
transport: U2 or U6 Stadtmitte, about 3 minutes on foot.
verify_notes: REGISTER: Naturdenkmal 1-102/B-2, listed as Bosnischer Ahorn, Latin Acer opalus subsp. obtusatum, designated 1993-03-02, reasons Eigenart, Schoenheit, Seltenheit, landeskundliche Gruende (most reasons of any in this batch). SPECIES/PHOTO CAUTION: sibling register row 1-102/B-1 (52.512392,13.392032, about 14 m away) is a Spitz-Ahorn (Acer platanoides). Commons has files titled Bosnischer Ahorn at 8 m (...Ecke Charlottenstrasse 2024-05-19 05/06) and files titled Spitz-Ahorn at 2 to 6 m (...suedwestlich des Deutschen Doms 2024-05-19 03/04/07) and a Schnurbaum file at 8 m; two trees stand close, so the photo pass must not assume which trunk a file shows; if unsure, photo status held. The pin is confirmed to the register point and one of the geotagged photos but a recognition line is needed because the neighbour is 14 m away. Also on the square: Japanischer Schnurbaum 1-10/B-1/-2 (52.512881,13.391817, about 50 m north, another Naturdenkmal, Styphnolobium japonicum, reasons Eigenart and landeskundliche Gruende) not delivered here. OSM has unlabelled natural=tree nodes in the square, not decisive. PHOTO CANDIDATES: Commons File:Naturdenkmal Bosnischer Ahorn Gendarmenmarkt, suedwestlich des Deutschen Doms, Ecke Charlottenstrasse 2024-05-19 06.jpg, CC0, Leonhard Lenz (also 05).
